item.title: In call with Israeli counterpart, PM Modi says urgent need to restore West Asia peace
item.description: PM Modi said he had received acall from Netanyahu during which the leaders reviewed the sustained momentum in bilateral ties and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the partnership. Modi did not mention Netanyahu’s invitation in his post on the conversation. “We exchanged views on developments in West Asia and underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region,” Modi said on X.

item.title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
item.description: PM Modi and his Polish counterpart Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.

item.title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
item.description: The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Sinha

item.title: Govt plans colour-coded driving licence for Indians, foreigners
item.description: Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash

item.title: Centre flags data gap, regulatory hurdles in curbing hospital mark-ups
item.description: The Union govt has told the SC in its affidavit that margins on hospital consumables can range from 100% to 1,000% or more, highlighting concerns over the high mark-ups patients often face on supplies used during treatment. However, a senior official told TOI that the govt does not have the data needed to assess margins across hospital supplies and determine whether wider controls are warranted.
item.dc:creator: Anuja Jaiswal

item.title: Movie glorifies violence, generalises graft in medical field: IMA
item.description: In a letter, dated Oct 22, to I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak sought an impartial review of the promo video for the upcoming film and appropriate corrective measures from its makers. It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of National Medical Commission.
item.dc:creator: Anuja Jaiswal

item.title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
item.description: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child “must be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort alone”.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Sonia Gandhi makes Instagram debut, shares first look of her upcoming book
item.description: In her first post on Instagram, Sonia shared a video of her welcoming the first copies of her autobiography “Belonging: A journey of love” which is set to be released on Nov 10. The video showed her holding up the book and then sharing sweets with daughter and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. “It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” Sonia wrote on the post.

item.title: Will decide on any notice to remove CEC according to rules: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla
item.description: Both the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha chairman had rejected previous notices from the opposition, saying their allegations “do not prima facie meet the high constitutional bar for removal proceedings”. Birla noted the process for removal of the chief election commissioner was the same as for removing a Supreme Court judge.

item.title: Resignation by Justice Yashwant Varma may end Lok Sabha proceedings
item.description: Justice Yashwant Varma’s name still figuring on the list of judges on the HC website had bolstered the view. However, sources said legal opinion, backed by a court verdict, that an HC judge’s resignation comes into effect as soon as he resigns may prevail in what was earlier seen as a legal grey area.
item.dc:creator: Rakesh Kumar

item.title: MEA calls out UN report for saying Dawood Ibrahim's D-company India-based
item.description: First secretary in India’s permanent mission to UN, Raghoo Puri, was responding to a report by Ben Saul, the special rapporteur on the ‘Promotion and Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms while Countering Terrorism’. He said this presented member-states with a fait accompli, an unfortunate situation for an organisation already facing challenges to its legitimacy.

item.title: Hospitals ‘overcharging’ is a malpractice: Govt to Supreme Court
item.description: In an affidavit filed in SC on the issue of capping prices of all medicines and medical consumables, chemicals and fertilisers ministry said that patients have a very low bargaining position with respect to hospitals, resulting in various malpractices. The affidavit noted the irony of India being home to companies making cheap drugs but patients here having to pay way above the manufacturing price, as well as patients being subjected to overcharging by hospitals.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Google India, Telegram executives appear before NCPCR over CSEAM
item.description: Meta has submitted its response following the appearance of Meta India chief Arun Srinivas and senior executives of the company before NCPCR last month over the inquiry instituted after it took cognisance of allegations concerning paid advertisements on Instagram that allegedly facilitated access to Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM)/CSEAM. Meta’s response is under scrutiny, sources in NCPCR said.
item.dc:creator: Ambika Pandit

item.title: 21 years on, double life term for Jammu terror attack that killed baby, 2 others
item.description: In his order on Wednesday, principal sessions judge Ramban Ajay Kumar Gupta rejected defence arguments that the attack had taken place more than two decades ago when Sharief was young, his long incarceration and possibility of rehabilitation. Besides the life sentences, the court imposed two separate terms of 10 years on Sharief under various sections pertaining to murder and arms act offences.
item.dc:creator: Sanjay Khajuria

item.title: Govt defends cancellation of Wangchuk institute’s land allotment, alleges role in last year’s unrest
item.description: The claims have been made in an affidavit filed on Wednesday in which Wangchuk is also accused of inciting “violence in Leh on Sept 24, 2025” in which four people were killed and scores injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood and Sixth Schedule status for the Union territory (UT) of Ladakh.
item.dc:creator: Naseer Ganai

item.title: Sonam Wangchuk accuses Centre of betraying Ladakh groups, alleges backtracking on May understanding
item.description: Wangchuk said the representatives of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) had come prepared for Oct 22 talks in Delhi as a follow up of the May 15 meeting in Leh, with the expectation that the MHA and Ladakh bodies' respective drafts on contours and powers of UT-level body and district councils, would be discussed.
item.dc:creator: Bharti Jain and Naseer Ganai

item.title: New norms to limit fuel leaks, protect EV batteries in rear-end crashes
item.description: In a notification, road transport ministry has also made the automotive standard, AIS-192, mandatory for Event Data Recorder (EDR) from Oct 2029 if it is installed in any car. The EDR feature is not mandatory for all cars, and it remains an optional feature. EDR records crash details, which help establish what happened immediately before and during a collision. It is similar in purpose to an aircraft’s flight-data recorder.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash

item.title: PM Modi calls for stronger global institutions; takes ‘failed product’ jab at Congress
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the need for stronger global institutions during his address at the NDTV World Summit. He argued that the current global system struggles to address new challenges, particularly in international relations. Modi also criticized Congress leadership for failing to effectively launch their leader, calling it a burden on the party. Furthermore, he highlighted India's role in international cooperation, especially during the Covid-19 pandemic.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.description: CDSCO says no bioequivalence study required for oral solution; company says labels on free bottles were part of standard packaging protocol
